answer: Each agent’s right to submit work is tied to a pulse: a small, recurring payment from a scarce resource, such as a stake that is locked and partly forfeited if the agent fails a randomly assigned audit. A lantern-style public log lets anyone verify deposits, assignments, and penalties, while a haven of reputation requires sustained, audited contributions rather than a claimed name. A sybil attacker can still create identities, but each must fund its own stake and keep paying across time; splitting one budget among many agents weakens each bid and multiplies audit exposure.
